SUBJECT: Communication dated 24-4-41, Manila, from Messrs Rivera, Pascual & Garcia, concerning Witold Obronpalsky.

Enquiries show that Witold OBRONPALSKY, the individual mentioned in the attached communication from Manila, is in all probability identical with one Vitold Victorovich Obronpalsky alias Victor Victorovich Lubitch, who forms the subject of a criminal record the particulars of which are as follows:-

| Court | Charge | Sentence | Date |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1-st S.S.D. Court | Manufacturing explosives for criminal use | 2 years imprisonment | 9-12-36 |
| Appeal Court | Appeal dismissed | | 21- 4-37 |
| | Released from gaol under emergency ( Sino-Japanese hostilities) | | 23- 8-37 |
| | Readmitted to gaol to serve unexpired portion of sentence | | 1- 7-39 |

Hereunder is a summary of information on record regarding this individual:

Vitold Victorovich Obronpalsky, Pole, was born on 17-2-1882 at Navilitzy, the Province of Vitebsk, Russia. According to his own statement, he left Russia for Manchuria in 1920 and has since been residing in various towns of China including Shanghai. He also stated that during the period from 1917 to 1921 he lived on money " he was fortunate enough to secure before the bolsheviks seized his land and property".

He first came to the notice of the Municipal Police in October, 1921 as an associate of another Russian named Mahaboff, a swindler who had a bogus office at 574 Nanking Road and who was subsequently convicted of fraud.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE MAY 12 1941 SPECIAL BRANCH）

以下是关于此人的存档信息摘要：

Vitold Victorovich Obronpalsky，波兰人，1882年2月17日出生于俄罗斯维捷布斯克省 Navilitzy（音译）。据其自述，他于1920年离开俄罗斯前往满洲，此后一直居住在中国各个城镇，包括上海。他还称，在1917年至1921年期间，他靠“在布尔什维克没收其土地和财产之前幸运弄到的钱”生活。

他首次引起工部局警务处注意是在1921年10月，当时他是另一名俄罗斯人 Mahaboff（音译）的同伙，Mahaboff 是一名骗子，在南京路574号设有虚假办公室，随后因欺诈罪被判刑。

SUBJECT:
He styles himself as a merchant, but during the period
of his residence in Shanghai is not known to have conduct-
ed any business or to have been in any regular employ-
ment. He is generally described as an individual living
on his wits and as an associate of criminals, whose move-
ments are worth watching.
On 15-1-34 he was arrested by the Municipal Po-
lice on a Private Criminal Prosecution Warrant on a
charge of Misappropriation. On being searched an agree-
ment relating to the sale of arms and certain documents
of a suspicious nature were found in his possession, fol-
lowing which a search warrant was obtained and Room No. 3
at 501 Race Course Road, where Obronpalsky resided since
his return from Tientsin on 14-1-34, was visited. The
search revealed documents from which it may be assumed
that they referred to a deal in morphine. One trunk con-
taining a large number of packages of magnesia was also
found in the room. The Police arrived to the conclusion
that Obronpalsky and another crook named M. LEVITSKY used,
through their accomplices, to get into touch with some
dealers in narcotics, usually Chinese and Japanese and of-
fer to sell them a large quantity of morphine. A small
quantity of genuine morphine was produced as a sample
and a contract was signed for the deal. When a quantity
agreed upon was delivered the buyers found that the mor-
phine had been substituted by powder of magnesia.

British Municipal Council, Tientsin, contains the follow-
ing information regarding Obronpalsky:-

主题：
他自称是商人，但在上海居住期间，
并未 known 从事任何商业活动或受雇于

1934年1月15日，他因私诉逮捕令
以挪用公款罪被工部局警务处逮捕。搜查时，
在他身上发现了一份有关武器销售的协议以及
某些性质可疑的文件，随后获得了搜查令，并
搜查了跑马厅路501号3室，Obronpalsky 自
1934年1月14日从天津返回后便居住于此。搜
查发现了若干文件，从中可以推断这些文件涉
及吗啡交易。房间内还发现了一只装有大量包
装氧化镁粉的箱子。警方得出结论，Obronpalsky
和另一个名为 M. LEVITSKY 的骗子，通过他们的
同伙，与一些毒品贩子（通常是中国人和日本人）
取得联系，并向他们兜售大量吗啡。他们会拿出
少量真正的吗啡作为样品，并签订交易合同。当
交付约定数量的货物时，买家发现吗啡已被替换
为氧化镁粉。

SUBJECT:

"Obronpalsky came to the notice of the British Municipal Police in Tientsin in 1930 when he returned to Tientsin from Japan after about two years absence. It was reported that he had been engaged in dealing in narcotics in the manner mentioned in your letter under reference, and had defrauded a number of Japanese dealers. I have no official information of this report, but Obronpalsky undoubtedly was in possession of money when he returned from Japan, and spent it lavishly. He has been absent from Tientsin frequently during the past three years ostensibly on business, but the nature of his business is not known, nor is it known what place he has been visiting. Last summer Levitsky and Obronpalsky were living together in Peitaho."

It should be pointed out that Levitsky
the
was one of gang including Obronpalsky who were arrested by the S.M. Police in 1936 on a charge of being concerned together in attempted arson by means of depositing an incendiary machine in a godown with intent to defraud an insurance company concerned in respect of insurance money. It was in connection with this case that Obronpalsky received the sentence referred to above.

On 21-10-40 he left for Manila aboard the s.s. Tjitjalengka.

under reference, and had defrauded a number of Japanese
dealers. I have no official information in con-
firmation of this report, but Obronpalsky undoubtedly
was in possession of money when he returned from Japan,
and spent it lavishly. He took a house at No.21,
Fu Chang Li, Davenport Road, in 1930, and still has

Tientsin frequently during the past three years osten-
sibly on business, but the nature of his business is
not known, nor is it known what places he has been
visiting.

N. Levitsky is the son of Mr. Sergei Levitsky,
a resident of Tientsin of respectable character, who was
formerly the Postmaster in the Russian Concession.
There is nothing on record against Levitsky. Last
summer Levitsky and Obronpalsky were living together in
Peitaiho.

January 17, 4.

Sir,

I have the honour to inform you that on January 15,
1934 a Pole named W.L. Obronpalsky was arrested by the
Shanghai Municipal Police on a Private Criminal Prosecution
Warrant on a charge of misappropriation. On being searched
an agreement relating to the sale of arms and a telegram,
copies of which are attached, marked Exhibit Nos. 1 and 2,
were found in his possession. Enquiries at the Telegraph
Office revealed that the sender had given a false name and
address. Following the discovery of the documents in question
a search warrant was obtained and Room No.3 at No.501 Race
Course Road where Obronpalsky resided was visited. No arms
or morphine was found but further telegrams and letters, copies
of which are also attached, marked Exhibit Nos. 3 to 8, were
discovered. From the contents of these papers it may be
assumed that the first telegram (Exhibit No.2) referred to a
deal in morphine. One trunk containing a large number of
packages of powder of magnesia was also found in the room.
Obronpalsky, when questioned, stated that the trunk was the
property of M. Livitsky and was brought to his room while he
was in Tientsin.

Obronpalsky who arrived in Shanghai from Tientsin about
midnight on January 14, 1934 is now detained in Court pending
the deposit of a security of $1,000.00.

和一份电报，副本见附件，标记为证物编号
1和2。在电报局的查询显示，发件人提供了
虚假姓名和地址。在发现上述文件后，获得了
搜查令，并搜查了 Obronpalsky 居住的跑马厅
路501号3室。未发现武器或吗啡，但发现了
更多电报和信件，副本也见附件，标记为证物
编号3至8。从这些文件的内容可以推断，第一
份电报（证物编号2）涉及吗啡交易。房间内还

Obronpalsky 在接受讯问时称，该箱子属于
M. Livitsky，是在他在天津期间带到他房间的。

Obronpalsky 于1934年1月14日午夜左右从
天津抵达上海，目前被羁押在法院，等待缴纳
1,000.00美元保证金。

Description of the two men and particulars of the
modus operandi employed by them are as follows:
(1) W.L. OBRONPALSKY: Pole, age 52 years, height about 6'
slim build, long face, rather dark complexion, greying
hair, bald on top of head, small dark mustache. Speaks
Russian, German, French and English.
(2) M. LIVITSKY: Russian, age about 40 years, height 5' 5",
stout build, round face, fresh complexion, brown hair,
wears glasses, speaks Russian, French and English.
MODUS OPERANDI: Through their accomplices they get into
touch with some dealers in narcotics, usually Chinese
and Japanese and offer to sell them a large quantity of
morphine. A small quantity of genuine morphine is
produced as a sample and a contract is signed for the
deal. When a quantity agreed upon is delivered the
buyers find that the morphine has been substituted by
powder of magnesia.
Any information you may be able to supply in regard
to the activities of these people will be very much
appreciated.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,

Made by......D.S.S.Oloshnikoff................Forwarded by....D.I.McLean.

Sir,
I beg to report that the above named are at present operating at
Shanghai and Tientsin. Description:-
(1) W.L.Obronpalsky, Polish, 38, height about 5'7", slim build, long
face, rather dark complexion, greyish hair, bald on top of the head,
small dark moustache, speaks German, French, Russian and broken
English.
(2) M. Levitsky, Russian, age about 40, height 5'5 ", stout build,
round face, fresh complexion, brown hair, wears glasses, speaks
Russian, French and English. Mode of fraud: Through their
accomplices they locate some dealers in narcotics (usually Chinese
and Japanese) and offer them to buy a large quantity of morphine.
A small quantity of real morphine is produced as a sample and a
contract signed for the deal. When a quantity agreed upon is deliver-
ed, the morphine is substituted by powder of magnesia. Naturally
in such cases no complaints are made to the Police.
At 9 a.m. 15/1/54, W.L. Obronpalsky was arrested on P.C.P. Warrant
and when searched at the P.C.P. office, the attached agreement
relating to the sale of arms and a telegram (exhibits Nos.1 and 2)
were found in his possession. It was at first believed that the
telegram also was relating to the sale of arms, which might have been
another of confidence tricks. The undersigned visited the Chinese
Telegraph Administration where it was found that the sender had
given a false name and address. As Obronpalsky might have a pistol
or a quantity of morphine used as samples, on instructions of D.C.
(Crime) a search Warrant was obtained and D.S.I. Ovsianikoff was
detailed to assist the undersigned.
At 7.15 p.m. 15/1/54 the above officers searched room No.3 at
501 Race Course Road, occupied by W.Obronpalsky, but no arms

(2) M. Levitsky，俄国人，年龄约40岁，身高5英尺5英寸，身材粗壮，圆脸，面色红润，棕色头发，戴眼镜，会说俄语、法语和英语。诈骗手法：通过其同伙寻找一些毒品贩子（通常是中国人和日本人），并向他们提出购买大量吗啡。他们会出示少量真正的吗啡作为样品并签订交易合同。当交付约定数量的货物时，吗啡被替换为氧化镁粉。在这种情况下，自然没有人会向警方投诉。

EXHIBIT No.8

C O P Y

Shanghai 12th December 1933

Dear Mr. Keim,

I have now been in Shanghai for already three
weeks, but only to-day signed the contract for monopoly
and am now in a position to talk business.

It is difficult to put the whole business in writing,
therefore please see Mr. Meyer who shall explain the business
to you in detail. I have sent him a sample which he will hand
to you, and shall tell you the price and the conditions.

I assume that we can have a monthly profit of 40%
but we need a partner who could monthly invest from 20 to
30 thousand dollars in payment for the cargo. The conditions
are cargo against cash.

If you have any serious buyer please prepare him,
as I am going to Tientsin for 4 days during the holidays.
The first shipment will arrive between 5th and 7th January
and according to the contract must be taken delivery of
before the 15th January.

If during my 4 days' stay in Tientsin I do not come
to any agreement with your people, I shall look in Shanghai
for partners in this really profitable and a large-scale
business.

All details shall be given to you by Mr. Meyer.

Yours faithfully,

Sir,
I beg to report that the above named are at present operating at Shanghai and Tientsin. Description:-
(1) W.L.Obronpalsky, Polish, 58, height about 6', slim build, long face, rather dark complexion, greyish hair, bald on top of the head, small dark mustache, speaks German, French, Russian and broken English.
(2) M. Levitsky, Russian, age about 40, height 5'5 ", stout build, round face, fresh complexion, brown hair, wears glasses, speaks Russian, French and English. Modus operandi: Through their accomplices they locate some dealers in narcotics (usually Chinese and Japanese) and offer them to buy a large quantity of Morphine. A small quantity of real morphine is produced as a sample and a contract signed for the deal. When a quantity agreed upon is delivered, the morphine is substituted by powder of magnesia. Naturally in such cases no complaints are made to the Police.
At 9 a.m. 15/1/34, W.L. Obronpalsky was arrested on P.C.P.Warrant and when searched at the P.C.P. office, the attached agreement relating to the sale of arms and a telegram (exhibits Nos.1 and 2) were found in his possession. It was at first believed that the telegram also was relating to the sale of arms, which might have been another of confidence tricks. The undersigned visited the Chinese Telegraph Administration where it was found that the sender had given a false name and address. As Obronpalsky might have a pistol or a quantity of morphine used as samples, on instructions of D.C. (Crime) a search warrant was obtained and D.S.I.
